correctness.rationale: For each star and fixed budget the two leader orbits exhaust every feasible set. Direct block diagonalization gives unit eigenvalues and roots of z^2-(m+1)z+k, including a separate k=m case. The difference of squared-propagator traces is e^{-2T}(e^{2alpha T}+e^{-2beta T}-2); alpha>0, beta>alpha, strictly positive second derivative and initially negative derivative prove exactly one positive crossing. Integration gives a single-minimum comparison with limiting sign (m+1-2k)/(2k). This proves the full positive-real-time classification, exact equality boundary, strict preference, and separated transition times. Uniform-on-compact limiting equations justify both fixed-budget limits. The bundled verifier independently constructed actual grounded matrices and passed 21043 finite comparisons; finite tests are corroboration, not proof.

value.rationale: This is an exact complete two-objective classification for all finite times and every budget on a natural star graph, not an isolated parameter substitution. Its structural novelty is that the instantaneous and accumulated-noise objectives have different sharp control horizons: for budgets (m+1)/2<=k<m, the accumulated-noise optimizer never includes the hub, even after instantaneous error switches to a hub. The fixed-budget large-star limits log(2)/2 versus tau0/2 quantify a persistent performance horizon gap. This precisely addresses the practical mathematical question whether short- or long-horizon leader choices coincide.
